script: "You need a doctor's note". I don't like calling in to work. I am a 26‑year‑old guy who hates missing cash. I'd only call out if I was seriously sick. I work in the service industry, and you know how that scene is. Managers guilt you into cooking for you while you're half‑dead. They'll say, "You don't get insurance—get a doctor's note." The audacity, right? One year, I got hit with a legit cough and couldn't breathe. I texted my manager for a day off and they shot back, "wElL yOu NeEd A dOcToRs NoTe Or ItS aN uNeXsCuSeD aBsEnCe." I was like, "Seriously?" Turns out I had insurance through my dad. I was still offended that they'd called me a liar, but I figured, I'll get the note, hand it in, and get the day back. So I went to the doc. Four days off, signed, stamped, ready to roll. Back to the job, I handed the manager the note and said, "Here's my doctor's note. I'll be back on this date." Fast forward a few months. I am sick again. I get a longer note. I even asked the doc to add a line about when I'd stop being infectious around the food. Now they never ask me for a note again. They know they can give me the one or two days I request, or the full week the doc writes. And here's the kicker: I won't work while I am sick if I don't want to. (I know, right?)
